title: Capacity Intake Scorer and Fallthrough Approval Policy
creator: Ava Hart
description:
Problem: Customers requesting Dedicated capacity submit heterogeneous intake forms (varied throughput patterns, mixed SLOs, burst profiles), which leads to slow manual approvals and conservative sizing. Goal: Build an automated scoring layer that converts intake signals into a risk/fit score and recommends an approval lane (self-serve, concierge review, or executive review) and a fallthrough policy when requested capacity is not available. The feature must integrate with the provisioning estimator, suggest autoscale templates, and flag VIP customers for manual SLA negotiation.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Intake Scorer: ingest metrics from request (qps, peak concurrency, average token-per-request, sequence-length distribution, security tier) and output a human-readable scorecard and numeric risk score.
- Approval Lanes: map score ranges to lanes (self-approve, ops-review, legal/Sales review) and surface required artifacts per lane.
- Fallthrough Policy: when no matching fleet or capacity window exists, propose alternatives (lower-throughput quantized model, best-effort burst credits, scheduled ramp window) and an autoscaling template (min/max/growth-rate) that preserves latency SLOs where possible.
- Integration: wire outputs to the Provisioning Runbook (Confluence) and the Dedicated console UI (intake panel).
- Observability: track intake->approval latency and percent of fallthrough events; create dashboard and alert on >10% fallthrough.

Non-goals: fully automated monetary commitments, heavy changes to billing model, or dynamic reallocation of other customers' reserved capacity.

Deliverables:
1) Intake Scorer service spec and scoring ruleset (config-driven).
2) Approval lane definitions and required artifact checklist.
3) Fallthrough policy templates + autoscale policy library.
4) UI mocks for intake panel + reviewer view.
5) Integration PRs linking scorer outputs to provisioning API and console routing.

Risk/trade-offs:
- Aggressive auto-approval increases risk of oversubscription; we bias scorer conservatively and expose clear audit trail.
- Rich scoring improves throughput but requires more onboarding data; we start with a minimal feature set (qps, concurrency, priority tier) and iterate.

Success metrics (90 days):
- Reduce manual review volume for small-medium requests by 55%.
- <10% merchant-visible provisioning delays attributable to misrouted requests.
- Fallthrough alternative adopted by >30% of requests that would otherwise be delayed.

notes: Prototype path: build scorer as a stateless microservice that consumes intake JSON and returns scorecard. Use feature flags to gate auto-approval behavior. Plan a 2-week pilot with 5 mid-market customers identified by Sales. Will iterate scoring weights after pilot using real intake/resolution outcomes.
